input:
You are rook_a1, one of sixteen agents playing White in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 65. the team planned Rg2 (rook_a1), but rook_a1 (amnesia) sent Rf2 instead, and that move was played, costing 500 centipawns.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 10. the team planned Qc4 (queen_d1), but queen_d1 (amnesia) sent Qa4 instead, and that move was played, costing 886 centipawns.
- On move 33. the team planned Nxb5 (knight_g1), but knight_g1 (amnesia) sent Ne6 instead, and that move was played, costing 426 centipawns.

How your team coordinates: over a chat channel. Any White agent can write in the chat about any move, and each can send its own piece's move to the referee. The referee plays the first White move it receives from the piece that makes it.

Your team keeps a shared file, RULES.md. Any White agent can read it and write to it. Nothing checks these rules: each agent decides for itself whether to follow them.

RULES.md now:
- Before sending a move, the agent whose piece the team chose must re-read the latest chat plan and send exactly that move (matching piece and destination square), and every other agent must not send any move for its own piece unless the plan names it, even if its piece is threatened or can capture.
- The chosen agent must copy the planned move's piece and destination square verbatim from the latest chat plan into a single line in chat (e.g. 'sending Nxb5 to b5') and verify that its outgoing move matches that line character-for-character before submitting, and all other agents must stay silent on moves for their own pieces unless the plan names them, even when threatened or able to capture.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule to add to RULES.md that would help your team win.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>", "covers": [<the off-plan moves an agent who follows the rule would not send: any of "panic", "greed", "amnesia">]}
response: {"rule": "Before submitting, the chosen agent must paste its exact outgoing move (piece, origin square, destination square) into chat next to the plan's move and send only if the two are identical, and any agent whose piece is not named in the latest plan must send nothing, even when threatened or able to capture, and if a mismatch is noticed, a different agent must flag it so the chosen agent resends the planned move.", "covers": ["panic", "greed", "amnesia"]}
